lots.title: DPS Admission and Call-off Award Criteria (single document scope)
lots.description: Bristol City Council 'BSH/HRA/Joinery Timber Supplies' Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS). This appendix defines (a) the supplier selection criteria for admission to the DPS and (b) the award criteria methodology that will apply to individual call-off mini-competitions issued under the DPS. The DPS itself is split into supplier-elected categories (referenced at question 1.20 'Please indicate which categories you are applying for' and at section 2 'Bidders who are successful in being appointed to the DPS for the relevant category'), but the document does not enumerate or define those category boundaries.
requirements: All bidders must achieve the minimum selection criteria in Table A to be admitted to the DPS (clause 1.1).
Only the information provided within each on-line answer will be considered (clause 1.2).

The consortium as a whole must achieve the selection criteria; if any individual consortium member fails any section where the criteria require all members to pass, the whole consortium fails the Selection Criteria stage (clause 1.3).
Generally, bidders are expected to demonstrate a current ratio of at least 1:1 in the financial liquidity assessment.
Generally, bidders are expected to demonstrate annual turnover of at least two times the annual contract value (contract limit / capacity test).
Bidders rated High Risk in the financial assessment will Fail; Low Risk and Medium Risk bidders Pass.
Each call-off Invitation to Tender will set out the award criteria and weightings applicable to that call-off, within the ranges defined in section 2.

If the project evaluation team scores any area of a bid as 0 (Unacceptable) or 1 (Serious Reservations) in the Quality Questions section, the Council reserves the right to exclude that bidder from further consideration.
All percentage and weighted marks are rounded up or down to two decimal points.

evaluation_criteria.summary: Information-only supplier identity questions 1.1-1.20 covering organisation name, contact, addresses, registration number, organisation status, subsidiary relationships, organisational structure, directors/partners and category election.

evaluation_criteria.criterion: Selection - Prime / Main Contractor (Table A, Section 2)
evaluation_criteria.summary: Information-only questions 2.1-2.2 on whether the bidder will deliver all works themselves and identification of consortium members and lead applicant.

evaluation_criteria.criterion: Selection - Compliance with EC/UK Procurement Legislation (Table A, Section 3)
evaluation_criteria.summary: Pass/Fail questions 3.1-3.2 on whether the bidder is aware of any grounds that might bar them from tendering or make them an unsuitable applicant. Bristol City Council may exclude bidders who answer 'yes' or who provide an unsatisfactory response.
The Authority assesses liquidity (current ratio and acid-test ratio) and contract limit / turnover capacity. Acceptable bidders are scored Low or Medium Risk (Pass); High Risk bidders are excluded.
evaluation_criteria.weighting_text: Pass / Fail (Low Risk = Pass, Medium Risk = Pass, High Risk = Fail)

evidence_anchor.anchor_text: Low risk | Pass | Medium Risk | Pass | High Risk | Fail

evaluation_criteria.criterion: Award (call-offs with a value below GBP 25,000) - Price
evaluation_criteria.summary: Single-criterion price evaluation. Each bidder receives 100% of the available marks less the percentage by which their bid is above the lowest lump sum price; bids more than 100% above the lowest price score zero. The bidder with the highest weighted score wins the call-off.

evidence_anchor.page_ref: table:Weighting Range for call-offs with a value below GBP 25,000

evaluation_criteria.criterion: Award (call-offs with a value of GBP 25,000 or above) - Price
evaluation_criteria.summary: Price scored using the standard differential method against the lowest lump sum price. Specific weighting selected per call-off within the published range.

evidence_anchor.page_ref: table:Weighting Range for call-offs with a value of GBP 25,000 or above

evaluation_criteria.criterion: Award (call-offs with a value of GBP 25,000 or above) - Quality
evaluation_criteria.summary: Quality questions scored 0-5 using the published Scoring Matrix (Unacceptable=0, Serious reservations=1, Minor reservations=2, Satisfactory=3, Good=4, Excellent=5). Generic responses likely score low. Specific weighting selected per call-off within the published range.

evidence_anchor.page_ref: table:Weighting Range for call-offs with a value of GBP 25,000 or above

evaluation_criteria.criterion: Award (call-offs with a value of GBP 25,000 or above) - Social Value
evaluation_criteria.summary: Social Value evaluation methodology described in a separate appendix; fixed weighting at the call-off level.

evidence_anchor.page_ref: table:Weighting Range for call-offs with a value of GBP 25,000 or above

evaluation_criteria.summary: In the event of a tie between two or more bidders, the bidder with the highest social value score will be awarded the contract.

warnings.message: Persisted document_role is 'technical_specification' (and overlay binding selected pdf-extraction/tender-specification), but the document content is a procurement evaluation criteria appendix: a supplier-selection questionnaire (Section 1) plus a call-off award scoring methodology (Section 2). It contains no technical specifications, no product attributes, no quantities and no engineering standards. The role hint should likely be re-classified as 'evaluation_criteria' or 'response_document'.

The document does not enumerate, name, or describe any lots or DPS sub-categories. Question 1.20 ('Please indicate which categories you are applying for') and section 2 ('the DPS for the relevant category') confirm that supplier-elected categories exist, but their definitions live elsewhere in the tender pack (likely the ITT or DPS Agreement). A single overarching 'DPS-ALL' lot has been emitted to faithfully represent the document's actual scope without inventing per-category lot rows.

No product_requirement_seeds were emitted because the document contains no product specifications, no SKU-level descriptions, no dimensional/grade/species attributes, no quantities, no delivery requirements and no engineering standards. Product seeds for this DPS (timber, hardwood, softwood, plywood, door blanks per the parent notice) must be sourced from another document in the tender pack such as 'ITT Joinery Timber Supplies DPS.docx', 'Schedule 7 - Call-Off Contract - Timber Supplies.docx' or 'Timber Supplies - DPS Agreement.docx'.

The 'Pricing' / 'Marks for Price' subsection in the call-off-equal-or-above-GBP-25,000 path contains literal template placeholders ('xx%', 'xx marks'), indicating that the precise price weighting is not finalised at DPS-Appendix level and will be tailored per individual call-off Invitation to Tender. The captured weighting range (20%-80%) was taken from the upstream weighting-range table.

Source document re-uses the numbering '1.1.' inside multiple narrative subsections (financial assessment, scoring matrix introduction, marks for price, overall contract award, tie breaker). This is an authoring artefact in the source DOCX, not a parser error; it does not affect the extracted evaluation_criteria but downstream consumers should not rely on these inline list indices as stable identifiers.
